summary: Send the required wildcard body (search + $and filter + timezone) on POST /contact/list, move limit/cursorId from the body to query params in both `contact list` and sync, and read URL-valued pagination.next wrapper cursors.
reason: Respond.io v2 rejects /contact/list with HTTP 400 unless search, filter, and timezone are ALL present in the body ('Please check if filter is provided'), so both sync and `contact list` failed outright. The spec also misclassified limit/cursorId as body params — the API only honors them as query parameters, so a body limit was silently ignored (every page came back at the server default of 10) and the `contact list --all` loop re-sent page one forever. Finally, Respond.io returns pagination.next as a full URL ({"pagination":{"next":"https://...?limit=100&cursorId=N"}}) whose cursor lives in the query string; because "next" is already a recognized cursor key, the name-based scan returned the entire URL as the cursor value.
validated_outcome: Before: sync errored on contact with HTTP 400 and `contact list` failed with the same error; with the body accepted, limit was ignored and the --all cursor never advanced. After: `contact list --limit 3` returns 3 items with status 200 and a full sync hydrates contact with zero warnings; the mirror row count matches an independent manual walk of the API's cursor pagination exactly (28 pages of 100, unique-id verified). Full suite 940 passed (4 new regression tests cover URL-valued and numeric cursors, the required wildcard body, and the body-vs-query param split); go build and go vet clean.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: The generator should carry required-but-defaultable body fields (Respond.io's search/filter/timezone trio) into syncResourceStaticBody and the generated list command's default body instead of emitting an empty body that the API rejects.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Any POST-list endpoint with required body members fails 100% of syncs out of the box while the spec looks complete.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: The profiler should distinguish query params from body params on POST list endpoints (limit/cursorId here are query-only) instead of assuming every declared input belongs to the body.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Misclassified pagination params are silently ignored by the API, capping every page at the server default and breaking --all/sync page advancement.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: extractPaginationFromEnvelope should parse URL-valued next fields inside pagination wrapper objects (pagination.next as an absolute URL) before the name-based cursorKeys scan, reusing cursorFromNextURL.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: The spec even declares cursor_field: pagination.next; because "next" is itself a cursor key, the name-based scan wins and hands the whole URL back as the cursor, so cursor sync silently stops after page one.
